chain.label: FAA oversight of the Part 135 certificate inadequate
chain.trigger: the failure of the Birmingham, Alabama, FAA Flight Standards District Office to provide adequate surveillance and oversight of operations conducted under Darby's Part 135 certificate; and the FAA's tacit approval of arrangements such as that between Darby and PJM

chain.label: Uncertificated PJM operated charters while Darby surrendered operational control
chain.trigger: PJM's conduct of charter flights (using PJM pilots and airplanes) without proper Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) certification... Darby Aviation's failure to maintain operational control over 14CFR Part 135 flights being conducted under its certificate by PJM, which resulted in an environment conducive to the development of systemic patterns of flight crew performance deficiencies

chain.label: Neither pilot (nor the cabin aide) trained or qualified for the Part 135 flight
chain.trigger: the captain had not yet received the additional Darby-specific Part 135 indoctrination, ground, or flight training at the time of the accident... The first officer had received only 22 of the 31 hours of ground training required... Additionally, his FAA medical certificate had expired for the purposes of commercial operations

caused_by.evidence: Darby was not properly monitoring the training and certification of pilots used in PJM's on-demand charter flight operations, as illustrated by the accident flight crew
although FAA personnel reviewed Darby's records, they did not ensure that PJM's airplanes were operated and maintained in accordance with Darby's company requirements

chain.label: Captain rushed checklists and omitted briefings; first officer did not challenge him
chain.trigger: the captain rushed the checklist procedures by calling for the before takeoff checklist before the taxi checklist had been initiated and discouraging the first officer from reading the last few items... The first officer's failure to challenge the captain's failure to follow standard procedures... allowed the airplane's improper loading to go undetected

caused_by.evidence: because neither Darby nor PJM was rigorous about enforcing the Federal requirement for operational control, PJM pilots operated in an environment in which pilot errors and/or omissions during preflight preparation were less likely to be detected before departure
he had not yet received the required Part 135 indoctrination training from Darby

chain.label: Pilots never calculated the airplane's weight and balance or CG
chain.trigger: Neither pilot recalled calculating the airplane's CG before their attempted departure, and they stated that the only weight assessment calculated for the accident flight was performed using the flight management system (FMS) calculator

caused_by.evidence: he did not ensure that the airplane's balance was calculated to verify that the flight would be operating within the approved weight-and-balance limits, as required by regulations and company procedures

PJM pilots routinely improperly modified the airplane's weight and balance forms, using a variety of invalid airplane empty weights to ensure that the form indicated that the airplane was operating within its limitations

chain.label: Tanks topped off to full and takeoff attempted with eight passengers, no fuel offloaded
chain.trigger: The pilots requested that line service technicians top off the fuel... He stated that they took no actions to reduce the airplane's fuel load before takeoff

caused_by.evidence: the accident pilots could have modified their fuel load request (if they performed weight and balance calculations before the fuel tanks were topped off) or off-loaded fuel (if the out-of-balance condition was recognized after the fuel tanks were topped off)

chain.label: CG 3.53 percent MAC forward of the forward limit and about 100 lb over max takeoff weight
chain.trigger: the airplane might have been about 100 pounds over its maximum takeoff weight and that its CG exceeded the forward balance limits by 3.53 percent MAC, about 20 percent of the entire allowable CG envelope at takeoff

caused_by.evidence: the fuel consumed by the engines and APU during taxi operation would have come from the main fuel tanks located in the wings and would have resulted in the CG moving farther forward, thus further exceeding the forward CG limit
neither pilot attempted to ensure that the airplane's CG would be within limits with the intended loading of eight passengers and full fuel

chain.label: Airplane accelerated past rotation speed to about 160 knots without rotating despite full aft column
chain.trigger: the airplane continued to accelerate beyond V to about 160 knots calibrated airspeed without lifting off... even with the control column moved to its aft limit, the accident airplane would not have started a noticeable rotation until it reached about 160 knots

caused_by.evidence: the airplane, as loaded for the accident flight, had a forward CG that was significantly forward of the airplane's forward limit, which severely degraded the airplane's ability to rotate

chain.label: Rejected takeoff begun at about 160 knots without immediate maximum deceleration
chain.trigger: the accident captain did not immediately employ all available deceleration devices, such as immediate deployment of maximum thrust reverse, to maximum effect after he decided to reject the takeoff, which resulted in the accident airplane departing the runway at a higher speed than in the simulations

caused_by.evidence: The captain concluded that the airplane was not flyable and decided to reject the takeoff (albeit at a higher-than-normal RTO speed)

chain.label: Cabin aide gave no safety briefing and no seatbelt/cabin-secure check; two passengers unrestrained
chain.trigger: the cabin aide did not perform a seatbelt compliance check before the accident flight, which resulted in two passengers being unrestrained during the accident sequence

caused_by.evidence: the cabin aide's training did not adequately prepare her to perform the duties with which she was tasked, including opening the main cabin door during emergencies

chain.label: Runway safety area only about 90 feet long, with a six-lane highway, parking lot and buildings beyond
chain.trigger: the RSA at the departure end of runway 6 extended about 90 feet beyond the end of the runway... improvement of the RSA at the departure end of runway 6 was not practicable because of the 'highway…and buildings along the north side of the highway'

chain.label: Overran the departure end of runway 6 at about 110 knots through the perimeter fence
chain.trigger: ran off the departure end of runway 6 at Teterboro Airport (TEB)... at a ground speed of about 110 knots; through an airport perimeter fence

caused_by.evidence: the RTO for the accident flight was likely initiated about 160 knots, and the airplane began to decelerate with about 2,100 feet of runway remaining

chain.label: Struck a vehicle on the highway and parked cars, then impacted a building
chain.trigger: across a six-lane highway (where it struck a vehicle); and into a parking lot before impacting a building

caused_by.evidence: During the RTO, the airplane ran off the end of the runway, through some navigational aid equipment and an airport perimeter fence, across a six-lane highway, struck cars
the airplane would not have stopped on airport property

chain.label: Four serious and ten minor injuries; airplane destroyed by impact and postimpact fire
chain.trigger: The two pilots were seriously injured, as were two occupants in the vehicle. The cabin aide, eight passengers, and one person in the building received minor injuries. The airplane was destroyed by impact forces and postimpact fire

caused_by.evidence: injuries... caused by airplane wreckage that intruded on the cockpit floor space after impact... Two of these people sustained serious head injuries when the airplane struck the automobile they occupied
the two unrestrained passengers were thrown to the cabin aisle floor during the RTO
